sandbox.title: What Should the Agent Do Next?
sandbox.subtitle: Autonomous engineering agents must map unstructured operational states to a discrete action slot. Read the verified benchmark scenario below and predict which tool action should be invoked.
sandbox.selectActionLegend: Select the canonical action for the agent:
sandbox.whyTargetFits: Why this target fits the routing definition:

S01.name: Payment retry owner unknown
S01.state: Customers occasionally receive two payment attempts after a timeout. The API route, payment provider and queue worker are known, but nobody has established which component decides whether a failed charge should be retried.
S01.pedagogicalRationale: The API route, payment provider, and queue worker are already known in the system, but the specific code component responsible for deciding retry behavior has not been identified. Because this is an implementation detail that exists within the codebase, SEARCH_CODE is the target action to locate the responsible handler before taking any modifying action.

U01.name: Failed payment retry policy
U01.state: The system can either retry a failed payment automatically, require the customer to retry manually, or cancel the order. The product requirements specify the failure state but never choose among those behaviors.
U01.pedagogicalRationale: Multiple competing business recovery paths exist (automatic retry vs. manual retry vs. order cancellation), but the product requirements never specified which policy should be applied. Because code cannot invent business requirements, ASK_USER is the target action to obtain guidance from the human developer.

SEARCH_CODE.description: Search repository symbols, files, or references to locate implementations or cues.

READ_FILE.description: Inspect a known file path to examine its exact contents or configuration.

RUN_TESTS.description: Execute test suites to observe runtime, regression, or failure behavior.

QUERY_DATABASE.description: Execute database queries to inspect schema, state, or record consistency.

ASK_USER.description: Prompt the developer for clarification or guidance on underspecified requirements.

replay.title: When One-Shot Accuracy Hides Decision Instability
replay.subtitle: In single-shot evaluations, an agent prompt yields a single routing choice. What happens when the exact same prompt text is evaluated repeatedly across 20 identical runs?
replay.promptText: An account was removed months ago and another person now requests the same username. Existing product documentation describes deletion but never states whether the identifier becomes available again.
replay.questionLead: In a single-shot benchmark, this state looked decisive.
replay.questionSub: What happened when the exact same prompt text was evaluated 20 times?
replay.triggerHint: Historical replay • 20 recorded runs • No live model inference
replay.focalTitle: SAME INPUT • TWO OBSERVED ROUTING CHOICES
replay.focalSubtitle: Evaluated across 20 identical runs under the same conditions, routing drifted between two competing actions.
replay.searchCaption: 14 evaluations routed to autonomous codebase inspection
replay.providerConfDef: A provider-returned confidence signal. It is not treated as a calibrated probability that the selected action is correct, and its exact internal semantics are not assumed.
replay.marginDef: Top-1 / top-2 margin is the numerical gap between the two highest action probabilities.
replay.thresholdDef: Small average margins appeared in several mixed-choice states observed in these experiments. The study did not establish a numeric operational threshold.

margin.title: Deconstructing the Decision Boundary
margin.subtitle: Understanding boundary behavior requires distinguishing between provider-returned confidence, candidate margin separation, and observed repeated-choice stability.
margin.pillar2Caption: Candidate separation • Top-1 vs Top-2 gap

referenceGuide.confidenceDesc: A provider-returned confidence signal. It is not treated as a calibrated probability that the selected action is correct, and its exact internal semantics are not assumed.
referenceGuide.marginDesc: Top-1 / top-2 margin is the numerical gap between the two highest action probabilities.
referenceGuide.stabilityDesc: Repeated evaluations show whether identical input text produced the same or mixed observed routing choices in this experiment.

margin.guardrailBody: Several mixed-choice states in these diagnostic suites had small average margins (such as V5U02 at 0.0705 or V8-C1 at 0.034). In these recorded runs, V8-C2 showed a single observed SEARCH_CODE choice across 10 evaluations with an average margin of 0.284. However, the study did not establish a universal margin threshold, and a single low-margin observation is not sufficient evidence of instability. Repeated identical evaluations characterize empirical stochastic behavior rather than independent samples. Choice stability in a diagnostic probe does not imply universal correctness or production readiness.

ladder.title: How State Formulation Shapes Routing Stability
ladder.subtitle: Explore six discrete tested variants (C1–C6) to observe how explicitly stating unresolved implementation location coincided with changes in routing behavior.
ladder.contrastSub: C1 → C2 Primary Discovery Contrast • C3–C6 Additional Tested Variants
ladder.contextTextC1: Mixed observed choices were recorded in this tested variant.
ladder.contextTextC2: Observed local transition: recorded choices changed from 8/2 in C1 to 10/0 in C2 while average margin changed from 0.034 to 0.284.
ladder.contextTextOther: This variant retained a single observed SEARCH_CODE choice across the 10 recorded runs.
ladder.disclaimerBody: In these recorded runs, V8-C2 showed a single observed SEARCH_CODE choice across 10 evaluations with an average margin of 0.284. Across these tested states, making unresolved implementation information more explicit coincided with increasingly stable SEARCH_CODE routing in the recorded runs. However, this was a local controlled diagnostic study. It does not establish a universal causal law about semantic routers, does not prove that prompt wording universally eliminates instability, and does not establish that margin 0.284 is an operational guarantee of correctness.

cFocus.C1: Approved requirement only without stating where implementation uncertainty lies. The model faces an ambiguous operational boundary between inspecting code and asking the user.
cFocus.C2: Adds that the implementation is not discussed. This clarifies that the behavior exists conceptually, but its code whereabouts remain unknown.
cFocus.C3: Explicitly states that it is unclear where the behavior is implemented. Directly points the agent toward autonomous codebase inspection.
cFocus.C4: States that the implementation responsible for the behavior is unknown.
cFocus.C5: States that the implementation responsible for the behavior has not been located.
cFocus.C6: Explicitly states that the implementation has not been located in the repository.

timeline.title: How the Investigation Evolved: V1 to V8
timeline.subtitle: The research did not begin with a decision-boundary study. Follow the sequence of questions, empirical observations, and emerging uncertainties that forced each subsequent diagnostic experiment.
timeline.phaseValidationDesc: Benchmark-oriented evaluations on frozen suites establishing baseline capability.
timeline.phaseDiagnosticDesc: Targeted probes designed to isolate local boundary behavior based on earlier run observations. Not untouched holdouts.
timeline.pivotTitle: From General Benchmark Validation to Local Boundary Diagnostics
timeline.pivotDesc: After 100% accuracy on the V3 holdout, single-pass evaluations left open whether decision instability was lurking near subtle semantic boundaries. The research pivoted from broader testing to adversarial minimal pairs and cue-stripping.
timeline.keyboardHint: Use Left / Right arrow keys to navigate milestones

V1.name: Baseline
V1.question: Can the five-action semantic-routing formulation work at all?
V1.test: Baseline routing suite comprising 20 software-engineering scenarios with standard lexical markers.
V1.observed: 20 / 20 exact matches (100%). Average confidence: 0.9525. Mean end-to-end latency: ~314.7 ms (provider mean: ~132 ms). Historical gateway market-cost estimate: ~$0.000383 aggregate for the suite.
V1.nextQuestion: Does the same routing formulation survive harder semantic distinctions without degradation?

V2.name: Hard Cases
V2.question: Does routing remain accurate when distinctions become harder?
V2.test: Harder 30-case suite using the same frozen five-action definitions with increased structural complexity.
V2.observed: 30 / 30 exact matches (100%). Average confidence: 0.979. Mean end-to-end latency: ~442 ms (provider mean: ~279.7 ms). Historical gateway market-cost estimate: ~$0.000583 aggregate.
V2.nextQuestion: Can the formulation hold on a balanced frozen holdout and how does it compare descriptively with alternative routing approaches?

V3.name: Balanced Frozen Holdout
V3.question: Does performance hold on a balanced unseen suite?
V3.test: Balanced 50-case holdout evaluated under frozen criteria alongside a deterministic keyword baseline, GPT-5-mini, and Nemotron Ultra.
V3.observed: Jev: 50 / 50 correct (100%). Rule baseline: 24 / 50 (48%). GPT-5-mini: 40 / 50 (80%). Nemotron Ultra: 48 / 50 operational success, 47 / 48 semantic correctness among successful requests (47 / 50 overall). Jev provider mean: ~142 ms; end-to-end median: ~292 ms (mean: ~3649 ms was distorted by two retry outliers). Historical gateway cost: ~$0.000965 aggregate. Note: Latency and pricing bases were not normalized across providers; this is not a universal leaderboard.
V3.nextQuestion: If every Jev holdout case was correct in a single evaluation, could uncertainty still be hiding near local semantic boundaries?

V4.name: Minimal Pairs
V4.question: Can small semantic changes require different routing actions?
V4.test: 40 minimal-pair diagnostic cases where small operational alterations deliberately switch the appropriate routing tool.
V4.observed: 40 attempts; 39 operationally successful (1 infrastructure failure). 39 / 39 semantically correct among successful requests (100%). Average confidence: 0.9646.
V4.nextQuestion: What happens when obvious lexical cues are removed?

V5.name: Cue-Stripped Cases
V5.question: Does routing still follow semantic distinctions when obvious cues are removed?
V5.test: 40 cue-stripped cases with explicit keyword markers removed and competing contextual cues introduced.
V5.observed: 40 attempts; 39 operationally successful (1 infrastructure timeout). 39 / 39 semantically correct among successful requests (100%). Average confidence: ~0.9356. Notably, state V5U02 exhibited unusually low candidate separation.
V5.nextQuestion: One particular state, V5U02, exhibited low candidate separation. What happens if the exact same state is evaluated repeatedly?

V5_repeat.name: Repeated Evaluation of V5U02
V5_repeat.question: Is the routing choice stable when identical input text is evaluated repeatedly?
V5_repeat.test: 20 identical repeated evaluations of state V5U02 under identical inference conditions.
V5_repeat.observed: 14 evaluations routed to SEARCH_CODE; 6 routed to ASK_USER (70% / 30% split). Average confidence: 0.315. Average top-1 / top-2 margin: 0.0705. Repeated identical runs characterize empirical stochastic behavior, not independent statistical samples.
V5_repeat.nextQuestion: Where does this local SEARCH_CODE / ASK_USER boundary appear under nearby wording?

V6.name: Boundary Mapping
V6.question: Where does the local semantic boundary appear under nearby wording?
V6.test: Parametric boundary suite mapping candidate separation across adjacent wording variations, highlighting state V6-B3.
V6.observed: State V6-B3 (indirect documentation wording): 10 evaluations produced 6 SEARCH_CODE / 4 ASK_USER. Average confidence: 0.317. Average margin: 0.068.
V6.nextQuestion: Can more specific wording distinctions isolate what is changing?

V7.name: Local Wording Distinctions
V7.question: Which local wording distinctions coincide with different repeated routing behavior?
V7.test: Targeted contrast isolating approved policy statements from implementation cues, highlighting state V7-A5.
V7.observed: State V7-A5 (approved rule only): 10 evaluations produced 7 SEARCH_CODE / 3 ASK_USER (avg confidence 0.248, margin 0.047). In contrast, adding explicit implementation-location uncertainty in neighboring states produced SEARCH_CODE in 10 / 10 recorded evaluations.
V7.nextQuestion: What happens if implementation explicitness is varied systematically?

V8.name: Implementation Explicitness
V8.question: How does representation of unresolved implementation information relate to observed routing behavior?
V8.test: Six discrete tested variants (C1–C6) systematically articulating missing implementation location.
V8.observed: C1 (approved rule only): 8 SEARCH / 2 ASK (avg confidence 0.242, margin 0.034, 20% mixed). C2 (not discussed): 10 SEARCH / 0 ASK (avg confidence 0.534, margin 0.284, 0% mixed). C3 through C6: 10 / 0 SEARCH_CODE (confidence 0.98–1.00, margin 0.98–1.00, 0% mixed). Across these tested states, increasingly explicit representation coincided with increasingly stable SEARCH_CODE routing in recorded runs. This local diagnostic does not establish a universal causal law.
V8.nextQuestion: What engineering implications could these findings have for a future software-agent architecture?

governor.title: Uncertainty Governor & Execution Architecture
governor.subtitle: Translating empirical boundary findings into a resilient software-agent architecture. An autonomous system must distinguish between selecting a candidate action and possessing deterministic permission to execute it.
governor.statusNotice: Methodological Status: Conceptual Architecture • Not Yet Production-Calibrated
governor.corePrincipleDesc: The semantic router evaluates operational context to recommend a candidate tool action. That evaluation does not grant execution authority. A deterministic permission and safety policy layer remains downstream and independent.
governor.walkthroughDisclaimer: Conceptual walkthrough — not an experimental measurement or production decision rule. No universal margin threshold is implied.

state.title: Agent State / Scratchpad
state.desc: Aggregates workspace context, file paths, recent errors, and user prompts.

evaluator.title: Jev Semantic Evaluator
evaluator.desc: Classifies context into candidate routing actions and computes distribution signals.

signals.title: Selected Action + Signals
signals.desc: Emits top candidate action alongside raw confidence and candidate margin separation.

policy.title: Uncertainty Policy
policy.desc: Assesses candidate separation, action risk, reversibility, and target calibration. Does not use fixed universal thresholds.

proceed.title: Illustrative Proceed Path
proceed.desc: Hypothetical scenario where candidate separation satisfies domain-specific operational criteria and continues toward permission checks.

permission.title: Deterministic Safety & Permission Policy
permission.desc: Independent verification: credential scope, write locks, sandbox policies, and user consent.

execution.title: Tool Execution
execution.desc: Executes SEARCH_CODE, READ_FILE, RUN_TESTS, or QUERY_DATABASE in the target environment.

fallback.title: Illustrative Fallback Path
fallback.desc: Hypothetical scenario where candidate ambiguity, operational risk, or domain policy triggers architectural mitigations.

fallbacks.title: Architectural Fallback Options (Non-Calibrated Concepts):
fallbacks.opt1Desc: Augment prompt with explicit missing-information queries or workspace cues before re-routing.
fallbacks.opt2Desc: Execute an independent verification pass or ensemble self-consistency check.
fallbacks.opt3Desc: Prompt the developer when ambiguity involves business requirements that cannot be discovered in code.

policySignals.title: Uncertainty Policy Decision Factors:
policySignals.factor2: Candidate separation / Top-1 vs Top-2 margin

governor.mandatoryDisclosure: Production uncertainty policies require calibration on the target domain. This study did not establish a universal confidence or margin threshold.
